title: Interleaved session ladder bench - quick sketch
content:
Quick experiment notes: interleaved session ladder vs baseline (small-batch)

Summary:
- Goal: measure latency (p50/p90/p99) and cost-per-1k queries for an "interleaved session ladder" scheduler that temporally interleaves short, warm sessions with longer sessions to improve packing and slot utilization.
- Motivation: observed bursty micro-session mix where frequent tiny interactions (2-8 tokens) drive a lot of p90 jitter. Hypothesis: carefully interleaving small sessions into laddered slots reduces tail without losing throughput.
- Status: early bench, synthetic workloads + recorded traffic replay from production day-2029-03-15. Not yet A/B grade.

Environment / setup:
- Model family: rw-34b-quantized (2-bit hybrid profile) to match target prod mix.
- Hardware: 8xA100-p4 (simulated slotization layer) — homogeneous cluster.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.9.2 + experimental interleaver scheduler (branch: bench/interleave-2029).
- Baseline scheduler: small-batch opportunistic (current default).
- Workloads: three mix profiles used in replay: "chatty-micro" (75% tiny sessions), "balanced" (40% tiny), "longform-heavy" (10% tiny). Each replay for 30 minutes at steady average qps to stress slot allocation.
- Metrics captured: p50, p90, p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec overall, dollars per 1k queries (cost estimate from runtime accounting), slot utilization (%), KV-cache hit rate (approx).

Important knobs for interleaver:
- ladder-depth: how many session windows are overlapped (tested 3, 5, 7).
- tiny-slot-preemption: whether tiny sessions can preempt (yes/no).
- packing-threshold: minimum remaining slot occupancy to accept new tiny session.

Raw results (representative) — balanced mix (40% tiny)
Table: scheduler | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | cost / 1k q | slot util | kv hit
- baseline small-batch | 45 | 210 | 820 | $3.10 | 62% | 18%
- interleave (ladder-depth=5, preempt=yes) | 48 | 170 | 560 | $2.95 | 75% | 23%
- interleave (ladder-depth=3, preempt=no) | 52 | 190 | 610 | $2.98 | 70% | 21%

Notes: cost calculation is naive - uses token charge + idle-slot amortization from runtime accounting. Interleaver reduced p90 by ~19% and p99 by ~32% in this trial while also improving slot utilization by ~13 points. Cost per 1k queries dropped modestly (~5-6%). p50 slightly worse for deep ladder with preemption on (because tiny sessions can wait to be interleaved into an efficient slot rather than being served instantly), but p50 is within acceptable SLO for this workload.

ASCII latency trend (p90) across time window (sample run)
Time -> 00:00 00:05 00:10 00:15 00:20 00:25 00:30
Baseline p90  |>===--==--===--==--===--==--===| (~200ms-250ms spikes)
Interleave p90 |>==--====--=--===--=--=--==| (~140ms-180ms reduced spikes)

Tradeoffs observed:
- Tail reduction comes from higher packing (more KV cache reuse and fewer cold slots).
- Preemption: enabling tiny-slot-preemption improves tail (they can jump to fill small holes) but can increase jitter for some long sessions if misconfigured.
- Ladder-depth: deeper ladders give better packing up to a point (diminishing returns after depth=5) and add scheduling overhead.
- Edge cases: longform-heavy workloads sometimes see marginal increased p99 when preemption is aggressive; needs safety gates (max-preempt-rate).

Micro observations (hand notes during run):
- At 12:03 into replay, observed a short microburst that baseline turned into a string of cold-starts — interleaver absorbed it into ladder slots with minor p50 impact.
- KV hit rate improvements are modest but visible; suggests interleaver is aligning similar session contexts into nearby slots.
- Slot utilization curve smoother under interleave; baseline shows bursts of 90% then idle valleys.

Cost sensitivity sweep (very rough):
- With quantization profile unchanged, raising ladder-depth beyond 5 increased CPU scheduling overhead, eroding cost gains. Sweet spot: depth=4..6.
- Enabling preemption with a conservative preempt-rate cap (10%) gives ~20% tail reduction for <2% cost increase.

Recommendations (next steps):
1) Run longer A/B with production traffic (72h) with synthetic seeding to recreate edge surfacing patterns. Tag customers that might be sensitive to p50 increase.
2) Add safety limits: per-tenant preempt caps, and long-session priority buckets to avoid pathological preemption.
3) Expand to multi-model scenario: verify interleaver behavior when mixing models with different token-CPU profiles.
4) Integrate with Optimize's cost estimator UI: surface ladder-depth / preempt knobs and expected p90/cost delta for devs.
5) Add more deterministic replay: include a recorded-week sample to observe weekday/weekend mix differences.

Open questions / risks:
- How do billing signals (customers with strict latency SLOs) respond to slight p50 regressions? Need to quantify % of traffic where p50 is critical.
- Interaction with KV eviction: does interleaver increase cross-tenant contamination of KV cache if tenant isolation uses shared slots? (policy angle).
- Scheduler complexity: maintenance burden vs gains — is this a short-term optimization or productizable knob?

Quick checklist for next run:
- [ ] Merge bench/interleave-2029 -> staging infra branch (PR 412)
- [ ] Tag 3 anchor customers for A/B (contact CS)
- [ ] Add observability panels for ladder-depth, preempt-events, per-tenant preempt counts
- [ ] Run 72h A/B with cost accounting per-customer

References / links:
- RFC: confluence:OPT-433-interleave-proposal (design notes)
- Jira ticket: INF-1987 (bench infra work)
- PR: github:infra/benchmarks#412 (scheduler impl)

Notes to self: keep this short. Capture the 4/6/2029 run results, push to confluence once A/B validated. If prelims hold, productize as "session-ladder" toggle in Optimize with curated defaults for chatty apps.

End of sketch.
